Virgin Birth (Doctrine)
VUR-jin BURTH
noun phrase (Christology)
The doctrine that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary, without a human father. Grounded in the prophecy of Isaiah 7:14 and the narratives of Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 1:26-38. One of the fundamentals of the faith.

📖 Biblical Definition

The doctrine that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary, without a human father — that Mary conceived and bore the Son while remaining a virgin, the conception being a supernatural work of the Holy Spirit. The doctrine is grounded in the prophecy and the Gospel narratives: (1) Isaiah 7:14, Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel (the Hebrew almah, rendered parthenos, virgin, in the Septuagint and cited as fulfilled in Matthew 1:23); (2) Matthew 1:18-25, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost... that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost; Joseph knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son; (3) Luke 1:26-38, Gabriel's announcement to Mary, her question How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?, and the angel's answer, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God. The theological significance of the virgin birth: (1) it marks the supernatural entrance of the eternal Son into human nature (the incarnation accomplished by the Holy Spirit's miraculous work, not by ordinary generation); (2) it is connected to the sinlessness of Christ (the holy thing born of Mary, conceived by the Spirit, free from the entail of original sin transmitted through ordinary generation, though the precise mechanism is debated); (3) it fulfills the prophetic promise of the seed of the woman (Genesis 3:15, the woman's seed, not the man's) and the Immanuel prophecy (Isaiah 7:14). The virgin birth was affirmed in the early creeds (conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary, the Apostles' Creed) and is one of the fundamentals of the faith (one of the five fundamentals defended by the early-twentieth-century fundamentalists against liberal denial). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine of the virgin birth against the liberal-Protestant denial (which dismisses it as legend or myth) and the rationalist rejection of the miraculous; the virgin birth is a historical fact attested by the inspired Gospel narratives, a fundamental of the faith, and the marvelous manner of the eternal Son's entrance into human nature.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The doctrine that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary, without a human father; Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:18-25, Luke 1:26-38; marks the supernatural incarnation of the eternal Son, connected to His sinlessness; one of the fundamentals of the faith.

VIRGIN BIRTH (DOCTRINE), n. phr. (Christology) Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the virgin Mary, without a human father; Mary conceived and bore the Son while remaining a virgin, the conception a supernatural work of the Spirit. Foundation: Isaiah 7:14 (a virgin shall conceive; almah/parthenos; cited Matthew 1:23); Matthew 1:18-25 (conceived... of the Holy Ghost); Luke 1:26-38 (Gabriel's announcement; the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee). Significance: the supernatural incarnation of the eternal Son; connected to His sinlessness; fulfills the seed of the woman (Genesis 3:15) and the Immanuel prophecy. Affirmed in the Apostles' Creed; one of the fundamentals of the faith. Held against liberal-Protestant denial and rationalist rejection of the miraculous.

📖 Key Scripture

Isaiah 7:14 — "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

Matthew 1:18 — "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

Luke 1:34-35 — "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

Galatians 4:4 — "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The virgin birth is a historical fact attested by the inspired Gospel narratives and a fundamental of the faith; the corruptions are the liberal-Protestant denial (dismissing it as legend or myth) and the rationalist rejection of the miraculous.

expand to see more

The virgin birth is held against the liberal-Protestant denial and the rationalist rejection of the miraculous. Liberal Protestantism (from the 19th-century higher criticism onward) commonly dismisses the virgin birth as a legendary or mythological accretion, a pious fiction not to be taken as historical fact; this denial was one of the marks of the modernist theology that the early-twentieth-century fundamentalists opposed (the virgin birth being one of the five fundamentals). The rationalist rejection of the miraculous denies the virgin birth on the a priori ground that miracles do not happen. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine: the virgin birth is a historical fact attested by the inspired Gospel narratives of Matthew and Luke, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah 7:14, affirmed in the early creeds, and constituting one of the fundamentals of the faith. The doctrine is theologically significant: it marks the supernatural manner of the eternal Son's entrance into human nature (the incarnation accomplished by the Holy Spirit's miraculous work); it is connected to the sinlessness of Christ; and it fulfills the prophetic promise of the seed of the woman (Genesis 3:15) and the Immanuel prophecy. The believer confesses with the historic church that the Lord Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary — the marvelous manner of the incarnation, by which the eternal Son took human nature in the womb of the virgin, God manifest in the flesh.
